fatal_errors: The proposed silicon addition does not reconstruct the target intervention: a 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder consolidated by SPS.
The proposed 1600–1700 °C processing range misses the target optimum of 1500 °C and omits the decisive SPS pressure, heating rate, hold time, and vacuum conditions.
No prior evidence is cited for silicon-assisted densification or for a SiO2-rich film protecting ZrB2 in a liquid plating-metal bath.
The assumption that SiO2 will resist molten plating metal is not chemically established; in molten aluminum, silica may be reduced or disrupted rather than remain a durable passivating barrier.
The experiment leaves the plating metal, bath temperature, exposure duration, density metric, and quantitative acceptance thresholds unspecified.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering goals and offers a controllable comparison, but it is scientifically and evidentially disconnected from the hidden target. The target uses a substantial AlFeNiCoCr binder whose liquid-phase pore filling gives maximum densification at 1500 °C, whereas excessive temperature causes binder loss and renewed porosity. The generated mechanism instead relies on elemental silicon segregation and oxidation-derived silica, with no evidence supplied and no treatment of the relevant molten-Al reactions. Its experiment could test the alternative at a preliminary level, but it lacks the specified molten-Al boundary of 700 °C for up to 12 days, quantitative density and toughness measurements, multiple processing-temperature controls, and sufficiently explicit falsification thresholds. It is therefore a novel but unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
